WITH production_files AS (
  SELECT file_id
  FROM code.files
  WHERE is_test = FALSE
    AND module LIKE '%connectors/base%' OR module LIKE '%connectors%' OR file_id IN (
      SELECT file_id
      FROM code.files
      WHERE package LIKE '%connectors%' OR module LIKE '%connectors%' OR description LIKE '%connector%'
    )
),
connector_symbols AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id,
         s.file_id,
         s.name,
         s.qualname,
         s.kind
  FROM code.symbols s
  JOIN production_files p ON s.file_id = p.file_id
  WHERE s.kind = 'class'
    AND s.qualname LIKE '%SQLDatabase%'
),
all_methods AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id,
         h.name AS method_name
  FROM code.symbols s
  JOIN code.headings h ON s.file_id = h.file_id
  WHERE s.symbol_id IN (SELECT class_symbol_id FROM connector_symbols)
    AND h.ordinal = 0  -- only top-level definitions in the class body
    AND h.name NOT LIKE '_%'  -- exclude dunder methods
),
db_methods AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT class_symbol_id,
         name AS method_name
  FROM all_methods
  WHERE class_symbol_id IN (
    SELECT class_symbol_id
    FROM connector_symbols
    WHERE qualname = 'SQLDatabase'
  )
)
SELECT class_symbol_id,
       method_name
FROM all_methods
WHERE class_symbol_id NOT IN (SELECT class_symbol_id FROM db_methods)
ORDER BY class_symbol_id,
         method_name;

request:
The production database connectors are the classes that directly subclass SQLDatabase (defined in auto_ontology/connectors/base.py), excluding any class defined in test code (every file under a tests/ folder counts as test code). For each such connector class, which public methods does the class define in its own body that SQLDatabase itself does not define? A method is public when its name does not start with an underscore (so __init__ and other dunder methods are excluded); anything written with def directly in the class body counts as a method, including properties and context-manager methods. Methods inherited without being redefined do not count. Return one row per (connector class symbol ID, method name).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), method_name (string).
explanation: The query identifies production files containing connector classes, isolates symbols that subclass SQLDatabase, and then captures all public method names from the headings table (using the 'value' column, which stores the method/heading name). It excludes dunder methods and filters out any method that SQLDatabase itself defines, leaving only the publicly defined methods unique to each connector class.

WITH production_files AS (
  SELECT file_id
  FROM code.files
  WHERE is_test = FALSE
    AND (module LIKE '%connectors/base%' OR module LIKE '%connectors%' OR description LIKE '%connector%')
),
connector_symbols AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id,
         s.file_id,
         s.name,
         s.qualname,
         s.kind
  FROM code.symbols s
  JOIN production_files p ON s.file_id = p.file_id
  WHERE s.kind = 'class'
    AND s.qualname LIKE '%SQLDatabase%'
),
all_methods AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id,
         h.value AS method_name
  FROM code.symbols s
  JOIN code.headings h ON s.file_id = h.file_id
  WHERE s.symbol_id IN (SELECT class_symbol_id FROM connector_symbols)
    AND h.ordinal = 0
    AND h.value NOT LIKE '_%'
),
db_methods AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT class_symbol_id,
         method_name
  FROM all_methods
  WHERE class_symbol_id IN (
    SELECT class_symbol_id
    FROM connector_symbols
    WHERE qualname = 'SQLDatabase'
  )
)
SELECT class_symbol_id,
       method_name
FROM all_methods
WHERE class_symbol_id NOT IN (SELECT class_symbol_id FROM db_methods)
ORDER BY class_symbol_id,
         method_name;
